description: Hi! We are Bestepe İdman Yurdu
summary: "They Are Not Forgotten" is an animated storytelling video developed by team Beştepe İdmanyurdu for the Space Memory Museum concept. It explores what humanity left behind on the Moon and Mars—and how those artifacts continue to tell our story. To address the challenge, our project transforms historical spaceflight data into an emotional visual narrative. We highlight Apollo 11’s 1969 Tranquility Base landing, where the Eagle’s descent stage, footprints, and a laser retroreflector mirror still remain active today. Moving 225 million kilometers to Mars, we showcase the Sojourner rover, built to last 7 days yet exploring Ares Vallis for 83 days, and the Ingenuity helicopter, planned for 5 flights yet achieving 72 flights at Jezero Crater. This project is important because although dust settles on their panels and their missions have ended, their stories continue to inspire future generations of explorers.
details: Our project, introduces the concept of a Space Memory Museum dedicated to highlighting and preserving humanity’s historical and scientific achievements beyond Earth. The project focuses on significant milestones in space exploration, including the Apollo 11 landing at Tranquility Base on the Moon, the Sojourner rover’s exploration of Mars, and the Ingenuity helicopter’s pioneering flights in the Martian atmosphere. Through visual illustrations, diagrams, and historical information, the project demonstrates the scientific and cultural importance of these missions and emphasizes the need to preserve space exploration sites and artifacts for future generations. By combining space science, history, and cultural heritage, our project aims to increase public awareness, promote scientific curiosity, and inspire young people to explore astronomy, robotics, engineering, and planetary science. Its creative and innovative approach lies in presenting space exploration not only as a series of technological achievements but also as an important part of humanity’s shared cultural heritage. The project uses a digital presentation format with illustrations, diagrams, and informative visual elements to communicate complex scientific concepts in an accessible and engaging way. During its development, our team considered the historical significance, scientific contributions, educational value, and cultural importance of selected space missions, as well as the clarity and accessibility of the information presented. Ultimately, our project seeks to encourage greater appreciation of humanity’s achievements in space and contribute to awareness of the importance of protecting our space heritage for future generations.
